source: Final USAF Physical Fitness Readiness Assessment Scoring charts, effective 1 Mar 26, as published by AFPC current as of 17 Mar 26. Governing publication: AFMAN 36-2905, Department of the Air Force Physical Fitness Program, 24 March 2026.
transcribed: Verified cell for cell against the AFPC charts current as of 17 Mar 26 by tests/verify_charts.py.

run_chart_anomalies.note: The surrounding rows step by 19 seconds, which would suggest 19:26 for the under 25 column. Both columns print 19:36 in the 1 Mar 26 charts and in the AFPC revision current as of 17 Mar 26. The table stays monotonic, so it is transcribed as published rather than corrected.

walk_2km.note: Maximum time to pass. Pass or fail: no points (AFMAN 36-2905 para 3.7.3).

altitude_correction.note: AFMAN 36-2905 Attachment 3. Applies only at 5,250 feet and above; below that there is no correction. The run correction is subtracted from the recorded time, the HAMR correction is added to the shuttle count, and the walk gets a replacement maximum time.

run_2mile.unit: seconds subtracted from the recorded time

hamr_20m.unit: shuttles added to the recorded count

hamr_levels.note: 20M HAMR tally sheet: which level each cumulative shuttle falls in. A raw count is what the chart scores, but the level and shuttle within it is what an administrator marks on the sheet.

body_fat.source: DAFMAN 36-2905, 24 March 2026. Table 3.2 for the standards, Attachment 8 for the tape measurements, Attachment 9 (male) and Attachment 10 (female) for the percent tables.
body_fat.trigger: Para 3.15.4.7: a secondary BFA is required for a member with a waist to height ratio of 0.55 or higher who is not meeting PFRA standards. It is taken on an InBody bio-impedance scale where one is available, and by the tape method of Attachment 8 where one is not.
body_fat.outcome: Para 3.7.2: the BFA is pass or fail. A member who meets the standard has body composition scored as an exempt component. A member who does not receives an unsatisfactory score on the PFRA.
body_fat.standard_note: Table 3.2. Male 26 percent or less, female 36 percent or less.

M.neck: Just below the larynx, rounded up to the nearest quarter inch.
M.abdomen: At the navel at the end of a normal relaxed exhalation, rounded down to the nearest quarter inch.

F.neck: Just below the larynx, rounded up to the nearest quarter inch.
F.waist: The natural waist, its narrowest point, rounded down to the nearest quarter inch.
F.buttocks: The point that protrudes farthest, rounded down to the nearest quarter inch.

measurement.height: Attachment 8 gives no rounding rule for height. The tables are printed at half inch steps, so height is taken to the nearest half inch, as it is for the waist to height ratio.
measurement.same_sex: Para 3.15.4.7 requires a same sex administrator.

defects.note: A dropped digit. The row reads 32 either side and the column reads 32 above and 33 below, so only 32 fits.
The column reads 34 at 25.75 and 34 at 26.25, and the row reads 34 at every greater height, so only 34 fits.
Monotonicity allows 18 or 19. The 70.5 column is identical to the 70 column at every neighbouring circumference and reads 18, and 48 is a one digit slip from 18.

body_fat.encoding: Each height column is a step function of the circumference value: it never falls, and it rises a point at a time. A column is stored as its value at the first circumference plus the circumference indices at which it steps up, an index repeated once per point gained. That is a third of the numbers of the full grid and makes a lookup a binary search.
